# Pinned AWS output-pagination captures

`capture.py` runs the actual AWS CLI 2.31.18 executable against a private
loopback peer. It checks executable SHA256
`87630ec5232080b737502f4098f4c9adbf820c01d23c63b62affcad50059ad0a`
before invocation. Expected output is never generated by ESS.

The fourteen cases cover `ListObjectsV2` with `text` and `yaml-stream`: full pages
without a query, projected keys, a scalar query, `--max-items 3` with no query,
projected keys or `NextToken`, and resume using a token independently produced by the same AWS executable's JSON output.
Each service page has two objects; page two requires the exact opaque token
`page-two+/=`. Captures retain stdout, stderr, status, request sequence and
response bytes. The JSON token-control observation remains in the fixture.
Replay keeps stdout exact except generated CLI resume tokens, whose decoded
JSON envelopes must match; only encoding whitespace and member order may vary.
The opaque service continuation token and all HTTP effects remain exact.

The capture clears inherited AWS/ESS/MC and proxy settings, uses fixture-only
credentials and literal loopback addresses, disables metadata discovery and
paging, bounds subprocess/socket waits, and closes every peer in `finally`.
It reuses the existing raw-socket capture helper without modifying it. No live
AWS resources or production credentials are required.

From the repository root:

```sh
PAGER=cat python3 apps/ex_storage_service_cli/test/fixtures/aws_output_pagination/capture.py \
  --aws /path/to/pinned/aws \
  --output /tmp/aws-output-pagination-reference.json
```

Committed fixture SHA256:
`5cd3d386576416d8f88cffde82a0ab1c3347a0384761204bafe1d2f332a1dc8f`.

Replay from the CLI app with
`mix test test/aws_output_pagination_differential_test.exs`. This is bounded
HTTP/1 loopback evidence; it does not establish every paginator/output/query
combination, live-provider behavior, or completion of M5/M9.
